question: According to Table 2D-6, what are the recommended minimum initial upper-case and lower-case letter heights for an overhead Street Name sign?
model_answer: Direct Answer: For overhead Street Name signs, Table 2D-6 recommends a minimum initial upper-case letter height of 12 inches and a lower-case (nominal loop) height of 9 inches. This applies to all types of streets or highways and all speed limits, because overhead Street Name signs generally require greater legibility distances for road users to properly react. Guidance (recommended): - "Letter heights on street name signs should be as shown in Table 2D-6." Table 2D-6 lists for the "Overhead / All types / All speed limits" row: Initial Upper-Case — 12 inches; Lower-Case — 9 inches. Support (informational): - "A minimum upper-case letter height of 12 inches with a lower-case nominal loop height of 9 inches is recommended for all overhead Street Name signs regardless of posted speed limit as Street Name signs generally require greater legibility distances for road users to properly react." - "The letter heights specified in Table 2D-6 are the combination of lower-case letters with the initial upper-case letter of a mixed-case legend," and the values apply to the roadway that each sign faces rather than the street named on the sign. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2D-6, whose first row ("Overhead / All types / All speed limits") lists 12 inches for the initial upper-case and 9 inches for the lower-case letter height; [Image 2] shows the same table in context on page 248 along with paragraphs 09 and 10 of Section 2D.45 confirming the 12-inch/9-inch recommendation for overhead signs. Citations: - Table 2D-6 (p.248) - Section 2D.45 Guidance §7 (p.248) - Section 2D.45 Support §10 (p.248) - Section 2D.45 Support §9 (p.248)
gold_answer: 12 inches for the initial upper-case letters and 9 inches for lower-case letters.
